top_story: A rare Iran-US understanding reached on 16 June to end military operations in Lebanon appears to have set the conditions for the 19 June Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire, with Trump publicly pressing Israel to accept the halt after a fresh flareup. The ceasefire follows weeks of strikes that left places like Nabatieh in deep grief, where funerals, ruined homes, and emptied streets capture how any pause arrives after severe civilian damage in southern Lebanon. This de-escalatory track sits uneasily beside the broader US-Iran confrontation, as Tehran’s March threat of regional escalation after Trump warned Iran’s power grid showed how quickly Lebanon can be pulled back into a wider conflict. The immediate picture is a fragile containment of the Lebanon front, but its durability still depends on whether Washington and Tehran can keep broader escalation from overriding local ceasefire terms.
